newsitem.title: USA: Suspect indicted in death of Ennis Cosby.
newsitem.headline: Suspect indicted in death of Ennis Cosby.

text.p: The suspect in the shooting death of Ennis Cosby was indicted Friday by a grand jury but a judge ordered the indictment sealed until next month.
The suspect, Mikhail "Michael" Markhasev, will be arraigned on May 1, when Superior Court Judge John Reid said the indictment against 18-year-old Markhasev would be unsealed.
Markhasev was arrested March 16 for the January murder of entertainer Bill Cosby's son and pleaded not guilty on March 28 in municipal court on charges of murder with special circumstances.

The grand jury indictment takes the case out of municipal court and into superior court, where Markhasev will eventually be tried on charges of murder with special circumstance, which could lead to the death penalty if he is found guilty.

The superior court arraignment, originally set for April 18, was put off until May 1 at the request of Markhasev's defence attorneys who said they needed time to see if necessary funding was available for them to continue the case.
Defence attorney Charles Lindner also made a request for discovery on Friday, asking the judge to order the District Attorney's office to hand over material in the case.
After the proceeding, Lindner said the defence team had so far only received one police report from prosecutors.

Lindner said he had not seen the contents of the sealed indictment. Prosecutors often seek indictments as opposed to pretrial hearings as they allow the full trial to go ahead without their strategy becoming known to the defence.
The 18-year-old emigre from Ukraine, wearing a blue prison jump suit, looked relaxed in court Friday.
Earlier this week, Lindner disclosed that a key eyewitness in the case "categorically eliminated" Markhasev from a police lineup.
Cosby was shot once in the head on January 16 while trying to change a tire on his Mercedes-Benz on a side street near posh Mulholland Drive.
